title: Goodness of Zero-Sum Labeled Cycles
summary: Experiments support the conjecture for cycles of length three; it remains unresolved whether the goodness property holds for qualifying cycles of general length.

formal_statement.body: In the attack graph $G$ used to identify vertices that yield valid equations for the round function $F_0$, determine whether every cycle $v_1v_2\cdots v_Lv_1$ of length $L$ whose vertex labels sum to zero and whose vertices use no messages in common consists entirely of good vertices with probability close to $1$. This statement is supported by experiment when $L=3$, but it remains to be proved or refuted for general $L$.

scope.domain: Structural cryptanalysis of FF3 using an attack graph for round-function recovery in a four-round Feistel scheme.
assumptions: The vertices form a cycle in G.
The vertex labels sum to zero.
The vertices use no messages in common.
parameters: G, the attack graph used to identify vertices yielding valid equations
v1 through vL, the cycle vertices
scope.unresolved_remainder: For general L, prove or refute whether every qualifying cycle consists entirely of good vertices with probability close to 1.

progress.summary: The source states this as Conjecture 1 and notes experimental support when L=3. The corresponding claim for general L is left to proof or refutation.
